members.statement_original: Suppose $X_1,\ldots,X_n$, $X_i=(X_{i1},\ldots,X_{id})$ is an i.i.d. sample of $d$-variate observations with joint cumulative distribution function (cdf) $F$ and continuous marginal cdf's $F_1,\ldots,F_d$. members.local_label: Section 2 — empirical copula process centered under the null
members.source_heading: Section 2 — empirical copula process centered under the null
members.statement_original:
In the interest of improved efficiency, Genest and Rémillard (2004), p. 347, propose to use the previous definition with a version of the empirical copula process that is centered under the null hypothesis $C=\Pi$, namely
\[
\mathbb C^M_{n,A}=\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n\prod_{p\in A}\left(\mathbf1_{\{\widehat U_{ip}\leq u_p\}}-U_n(u_p)\right),
\]
where $U_n=U_n(t)=\min\{\lfloor(n+1)t\rfloor/n,1\}$ denotes the cdf of a random variable that is uniformly distributed on $\{1/(n+1),\ldots,n/(n+1)\}$.

name: Cramér-von-Mises statistics
type_shape: Squared integrated centered product process, with its exact all-pairs rank formula including diagonal terms. The differently centered bar-S statistic is not substituted.
semantic_boundary: Squared integrated centered product process, with its exact all-pairs rank formula including diagonal terms. The differently centered bar-S statistic is not substituted.

members.statement_original:
The respective Cramér-von-Mises statistics may then be calculated explicitly, and one obtains:
\[
S^M_{n,A}=\int_{[0,1]^{|A|}}\{\mathbb C^M_{n,A}(u)\}^2\,d\Pi_A((u_j)_{j\in A})=\frac1n\sum_{i,j=1}^n\prod_{p\in A}I^{(p)}_{i,j},\tag{2.1}
\]
where
\[
I^{(p)}_{i,j}=\frac{2n+1}{6n}+\frac{R_{ip}(R_{ip}-1)}{2n(n+1)}+\frac{R_{jp}(R_{jp}-1)}{2n(n+1)}-\frac{\max(R_{ip},R_{jp})}{n+1}.
\]

name: Expectation · Variance
type_shape: Finite-sample mean and variance under H_k of the selected subset statistic. These are not empirical sample moments or moments under an arbitrary alternative.
semantic_boundary: Finite-sample mean and variance under H_k of the selected subset statistic. These are not empirical sample moments or moments under an arbitrary alternative.

members.local_label: Section 2 — null expectation and variance, equation (2.2)
members.source_heading: Section 2 — null expectation and variance, equation (2.2)
members.statement_original:
For the purpose of aggregating over various index sets $A$, it is helpful to calculate expectation and variance of $S^M_{n,A}$. For $A\subset\{2,\ldots,d\}$ such that $|A|=k\in\{2,\ldots d\}$, let
\[
\mu_n(k):=\mathbb E_{H_k}\left[S^M_{n,A}\right],\qquad\sigma_n^2(k):=\operatorname{Var}_{H_k}(S^M_{n,A}),\tag{2.2}
\]
where $\mathbb E_{H_k}$ denotes expectation under $H_k$.

name: Aggregation
type_shape: Unweighted sum of the subset Cramer-von-Mises statistics over all k-element subsets, for fixed k between 2 and m. This is not the further normalized sum in Corollary 3.2.
semantic_boundary: Unweighted sum of the subset Cramer-von-Mises statistics over all k-element subsets, for fixed k between 2 and m. This is not the further normalized sum in Corollary 3.2.

members.statement_original:
More precisely, for some given $k\in\{2,\ldots,m\}$, we consider the following aggregation over all sets $A\subset\{1,\ldots,d\}$ with $|A|=k$:
\[
T_n(k)=\sum_{\substack{A\subset\{1,\ldots,d\}\\|A|=k}}S^M_{n,A}.\tag{3.1}
\]
